I will keep the whole 5.0 mu in cotton, same as before, because on my scale changing crops adds risk and does not help me much. I have only two people in the house, so I will manage for steady yield, not for fancy experimentation. With well irrigation, I do not need to gamble on rainfall, so I will feed the crop for a solid yield target and then hold it with water at the key stages. I will use an improved cotton variety, not old saved seed, because better seed gives me more uniform plants and makes the field easier to manage. On fertilizer, I will not cut too hard. Cotton needs a stable base, and if I underfeed early, I cannot easily recover later. I will aim around 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu for the season. That is enough to push yield on my land without spending like a big farmer. I will plough before planting because I want the root zone loose and I want the base fertilizer worked in properly. For irrigation, I will plan on 4 times: once after establishment if the soil is dry, then around squaring, flowering, and boll setting. For pests, I will assume 5 spray rounds in the year, because cotton here will not stay clean by itself. I do not spray blindly, but I will not wait until damage is obvious either. My target is about 320 kg per mu if weather stays normal and I do the water and pest work on time.
